messages:
mira: heads-up — saw an OOM on canary with a long-convo job (~45k tokens) hitting the KV layer. runtime picked a large kernel path, then kvcache filled and paging spiraled. stack attached below.

alex: ugh, can you paste the tail of the logs / alloc snapshot?

mira: sure — gist of the alloc trace:
```
[2026-03-10T14:22:03Z] kv_alloc: attempted 1.2GB, avail 0.8GB -> soft OOM trigger
[2026-03-10T14:22:03Z] kvcache: fragmentation 37% (slabmap hot shards)
[2026-03-10T14:22:03Z] paging: started eviction cycle, prefetched pages 1200 -> spike in vmem
[2026-03-10T14:22:04Z] kernel-select: stayed on fp16-kernel (low-latency) despite high seq len
[2026-03-10T14:22:05Z] runtime: oom: kv reserve failed for request id=ctx-5892
```

mira: interesting bit — the kernel selector didn't switch to the memory-optimized path because batch heuristic favored latency. that combined with heavy prefix reuse caused many small allocations and slab fragmentation.

jen: is this reproducible locally with the longctx sim? any flamegraphs?

mira: repro is fairly stable with the longctx harness (use profile flag). attaching perf hotspots summary:
```
hotspots: kvcache::alloc_slice 48%
         slabmap::coalesce 22%
         kernel::kv_copy 12%
         allocator::try_reserve 10%
```

leo: quick thought — we should try a short-term mitigation: per-request "kv grace period" that allows trimming oldest prefixes when free < X, and a reservation token so allocator can preemptively say no before attempting big kernel ops. this would let us gracefully degrade to a trimmed state rather than hit hard OOM.

paul: +1 for reservation tokens. also consider adding a soft throttle to the kernel selector: if estimated kv working set > threshold, prefer memory-saver kernel even at ~5-10% latency penalty. that avoids the burst of allocations during kernel switch.

alex: can we implement a cheap heuristic: estimate kv_wset = avg_prefix_len * active_prefixes, and if kv_wset > 0.8*kv_capacity then set a flag that forces compact-copy kernel and disables aggressive prefetch?

mira: yes — we prototyped exactly that in the perf branch. quick pseudocode:
```
if (estimated_wset > capacity * 0.8) {
  kernel_path = memory_optimized;
  prefetch_budget = max(1, prefetch_budget/4);
  enable_grace_trim(); // truncate oldest prefixes up to 25% until under cap
}
```

mira: results on canary: before patch p99 OOM rate 0.6/hr; after patch on same traffic p99 OOM -> 0.02/hr, median latency increased ~3% for those requests that hit fallback.

jen: sweet — any correctness tradeoffs on output? trimming prefixes might change completions for deep dialogs. need to flag in response metadata when trimming occurs so apps can opt-in to stricter guarantees.

leo: agree. add a response header `x-rw-kv-trimmed: true|false` and include trimmed token range. customers can then decide to re-run with a longer context or use a recall API.

paul: rollout plan? canary -> small dedicated -> 100% host. include runtime telemetry: trim_count, avg_trim_tokens, reservation_failures, kernel_force_count.

mira: deploying canary patch now. deploy-bot: @channel deploy started for runtime/longctx-grace-trim (sha: b3f1c2).

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded on canary (srv-rw-canary-2).

alex: after canary, let's run a 48h soak with the longctx workload and compare cost deltas. if everything stable we can enable for Dedicated as opt-in and then default after a week.

mira: noted. I'll open a brief playbook doc with exact thresholds, telemetry events, and rollback steps. TL;DR: adaptive kernel switch + prefetch throttle + kv-grace-trim + reservation tokens appears to eliminate the OOM spike while keeping latency acceptable.

jen: thanks — this looks promising. keep thread updated with soak metrics. :thumbsup:
